details.publicNotes:
For many, winter is a time of quiet, darkness, and privation. These are not the aspects of the season championed by the cheerful (if shy) hibernals. These fey are drawn to the feasts and spectacles that light up the gloomier months of the year, and an "audience" of hibernals can often be found clustered around the edge of a midwinter festival, soaking in the fellow feeling and good cheer. They are uniquely captivated by an outstanding performance, whether that be a rousing seasonal song or the dance of lights in the heavens common to poleward lands.

Outside of festival times, hibernals can typically be found roaming the winter wildernesses and aiding lost travelers or starving animals with their magic. They are rarely given to anger, preferring to sort disputes through challenges of song and dance, but they make an exception for those who seek to snuff out the light of joyful celebration. When conflicts arise, they demonstrate remarkable bravery, wielding a baton of hard ice as a weapon and using their swiftness to outmaneuver their stumbling foes.

Seasonals are a cycle of four kinds of fey, each tied to one of the four seasons: vernals who embody spring's renewal and storming showers, aestivals who embody summer's lazy heat and burning passion, autumnals who embody the melancholy culling and reaping harvest of autumn, and hibernals who embody winter's quiet cheer.

Whatever the current season in the mortal world, seasonals wrap themselves in a metaphysical cloak of their own season's magic and carry the songs full of that season's surging emotions with them wherever they go in the mortal world or across the realm of Faerie. Whenever seasonals meet, shy hibernals typically prefer to amuse themselves by watching the antics of the other three kinds of fey, while vernals impatiently call for energetic contests, aestivals languidly nap until roused to fiery bursts of activity, and autumnals attempt to imbue a sense of stark responsibility in the rest of their compatriots. Exceptions exist, with those seasonals interacting with the others in ways unexpected based upon the stereotypes of their season.

Frozen Fellowship

When a hibernal walks, icy gusts and snowdrifts follow in their wake—a disadvantage to those who would like to be invited inside to share cheer. Knowing that few mortals enjoy the cold that they bring with them, hibernals make sure to stay outside, enjoying cozy mortal festivals from afar. In turn, some folks bring their feasts outside, braving the cold in order to share fellowship with their frozen fey friends.

description.value:
You create enough food to feed six Medium creatures for a day. This food is bland and unappealing, but it is nourishing. After 1 day, if no one has eaten the food, it decays and becomes inedible. Most Small creatures eat one-quarter as much as a Medium creature (one-sixteenth as much for most Tiny creatures), and most Large creatures eat 10 times as much (100 times as much for Huge creatures and so on).

Heightened (4th) You can feed 12 Medium creatures.

Heightened (6th) You can feed 50 Medium creatures.

Heightened (8th) You can feed 200 Medium creatures.

You shield the target against dangerous temperatures. Choose severe cold or heat. The target is protected from the temperature you chose (but not extreme cold or heat).

Heightened (3rd) The target is protected from severe cold and severe heat.

Heightened (5th) The target is protected from severe cold, severe heat, extreme cold, and extreme heat.

You surround yourself in a beautiful melody that echoes in unusual directions, confounding attempts to hear your precise location. While using songshroud, you can't become unnoticed by creatures that can hear. You are @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.iU0fEDdBp3rXpTMC]{Hidden} to creatures that rely purely on echolocation or other sound-based senses, and you can't become observed by those senses unless they use magic or another special ability and succeed at a counteract check against this spell; as such, you can use songshroud in combination with becoming @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.zJxUflt9np0q4yML]{Invisible} (or foiling vision in a different way) to avoid being observed by a creature with both vision and echolocation. The shroud also protects you from harmful sounds, granting you a +1 status bonus to saving throws against auditory effects and resistance 5 to sonic damage. When you speak, you can choose to either project your voice normally or to use the song to hide it. If you choose to hide it, creatures that are farther than 5 feet away must succeed at a Perception check against your spell DC to overhear what you are saying.

@UUID[Compendium.battlezoo-bestiary-es-pf2e.sf2e-effects.Item.h0eng2GtJpOuRndn]{Spell Effect: Songshroud}

Heightened (4th) The resistance to sonic damage increases to 10, the duration increases to 10 minutes, and the status bonus on saving throws against auditory effects increases to +2.

Heightened (7th) The resistance to sonic damage increases to 15, the duration increases to 10 minutes, and the status bonus on saving throws against auditory effects increases to +3.

You conjure a cluster of sharpened icicles in the air before letting them fall. All creatures in the area take 1d6 piercing damage and 1d6 cold damage, with a basic Reflex save. Creatures that fail the saving throw are frozen 2.

Heightened (+1) The damage increases by 1d6 piercing and 1d6 cold.

A violent wind issues forth from your palm, blowing from the point where you are when you Cast the Spell to the line's opposite end. The wind extinguishes small non-magical fires, disperses fog and mist, blows objects of light Bulk or less around, and pushes larger objects. Large or smaller creatures in the area must attempt a Fortitude save. Large or smaller creatures that later move into the gust must attempt the save on entering.

Critical Success The creature is unaffected.

Success The creature can't move against the wind.

Failure The creature is knocked @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.j91X7x0XSomq8d60]{Prone}. If it was flying, it takes the effects of critical failure instead.

Critical Failure The creature is pushed 30 feet in the wind's direction, knocked prone, and takes 2d6 bludgeoning damage.

duration.value: until the start of your next turn

description.value:
An orb of biting cold coalesces around your target, freezing its body. The target takes 2d4 cold damage with a basic Fortitude save. On a critical failure, the target also gains weakness 1 to bludgeoning until the start of your next turn.

@UUID[Compendium.sf2e.spell-effects.Item.DdqWMj7cuf4S1bgr]{Spell Effect: Frostbite}

Heightened (+1) The damage increases by 1d4 and the weakness on a critical failure increases by 1.

You stir up the air around you to propel yourself toward a foe, then slice into them with blades of air. Stride up to half your Speed toward a target, then make a melee spell attack roll against the target's AC. If you hit, the target takes 2d4 slashing damage (double damage on a critical hit).

Heightened (+1) The damage increases by 1d4.
Snow doesn't impair the hibernal's vision; they ignore concealment from snowfall.
A hibernal's passage leaves snowdrifts in their wake, making any square they move through difficult terrain to any non-hibernal until the start of their next turn.

The hibernal takes a –2 circumstance penalty to their Will saves and DCs against mental effects with the auditory or visual traits, as well as against attempts to @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.AdPVz7rbaVSRxHFg]{Fascinate} them.

Trigger The hibernal takes damage from a physical attack

Effect The damage is reduced by 5 and the hibernal can immediately Step. If the attack was a melee Strike made from an adjacent square, the attacker takes @Damage[5[cold]] damage.

The hibernal Strides or Flies. Any creature adjacent to them at any point during the movement takes @Damage[4d6[cold]] damage (@Check[fortitude|dc:17|basic] save). They can't use Wintry Gust again for [[/gmr 1d4 #Recharge Wintry Gust]]{1d4 rounds}.
